This difficulty has led to an extreme line of work that bypasses manual partitioning altogether by taking raw bytes directly as inputs, including ByT5 (Xue et al., 2022) for text and ByteFormer (Horton et al., 2024) for multiple modalities. Representational objects, by contrast, represent the output semantic entities. They are independent of how inputs are partitioned, but instead reflect the requirements of downstream applications, ranging from atomic components for tagging to macroscopic wholes for search. Five forms of representational objects recur across modalities, and Table 2 summarizes the trade-off each entails. global vector Rd is one point per input, ideal for retrieval and classification, but it entangles every piece of evidence into single coordinate and discards location, multiplicity, and correspondence. sequence of local vectors RNdthe ViT patch features, the wav2vec frame features, the tabular cell statespreserves spatial or temporal tessellation for dense prediction and late interaction, at the price of storage and comparison cost (Akbik et al., 2018; Iida et al., 2021; Faysse et al., 2025). set of discrete codes {1, . . . , K}LVQ-VAE indices, audio codec tokens, HuBERT cluster assignments is the bridge by which audio and part of vision entered the language-model ecosystem (van den Oord et al., 2017; Hsu et al., 2021; Défossez et al., 2023). probability distribution p(z x)the latent of Omnimodal Embeddings VAE or probabilistic cross-modal retrieverrepresents the multiplicity and uncertainty that single point cannot (Kingma & Welling, 2014; Chun et al., 2021). And magnitude-preserving vectors retain the numerical level of the signal, so that temperature of 30 and 3 remain distinguishable property time series needs and no vocabulary can enumerate (Lin et al., 2024). No object is universally best: the representational object is the principal axis along which modalities differ even as their encoders and objectives converge, and it is why stronger encoder is not the same thing as better embedding. 5.2 The Granularity Shiftand Why It Is Partially Reversible The convergence of this chapter is that each modalitys preferred representational object is climbing upward, from local parts to whole semantic units. Representation learning has repeatedly globalized local states: word and token features pooled into sentence or document vectors, visual patches into image vectors, acoustic frames into utterance vectors, neighborhoods into node states and nodes into graph vectors, temporal samples into window or series states, and table cells into rowcolumn or whole-table vectors. Globalization supplies invariance, fixed-size indexing, and efficient comparison, and it is the third convergent axis of Part II. The shift is most legible in text, where it is also the oldest. NLP embeddings climbed the unit inventory one rung at time: from token-level static embeddings that placed each word at single point independent of context (Mikolov et al., 2013; Pennington et al., 2014) to sentence-level contextual and contrastive embeddings that pool whole sentence into one vector (Reimers & Gurevych, 2019; Gao et al., 2021), and on to retrieval-level dense embeddings designed so that an entire query or passage is single searchable point (Karpukhin et al., 2020; Izacard et al., 2022; Wang et al., 2022a). Each step pooled finer units into coarser, semantics-bearing object, and each step was motivated by the same insight: the most directly comparable representation encodes local descriptors and patcha whole semantic unit, not its parts. Vision traces the same arc: level objectives give way to whole-image readoutsimage-level contrast (Chen et al., 2020b) and masked patch reconstruction (He et al., 2022)and now to regionand set-level readouts that retain correspondence when the task needs it (Faysse et al., 2025). Audio moved from frame-level masked prediction (Baevski et al., 2020) to utteranceand clip-level discrimination and cross-modal alignment (Elizalde et al., 2023). Time series moved from point-level classification to window/patchlevel modeling (Nie et al., 2023) and series-level universal representations (Yue et al., 2022; Goswami et al., 2024), and graph embeddings from node-level proximity to subgraphand graph-level readouts (Goyal & Ferrara, 2018; Khoshraftar & An, 2024). The pattern is general enough to read as law: as literature matures, the granularity at which it embeds climbs from measurable atom toward semantic whole. The shift is not, however, monotonic toward universally better unit. The pooling operation that drives it upward can discard the locations, counts, ordering, uncertainty, factor identity, or relations needed by the next task, so modern systems move in both directions. Dense and region-level vision features preserve correspondence (Faysse et al., 2025); video systems retain temporally aligned clip representations for localization and retrieval (Xu et al., 2021a); audio diarization requires frame-wise speaker identity through overlapped speech (Fujita et al., 2019); graph systems expose nodes or subgraphs alongside whole-graph summaries (Perozzi et al., 2014; Xu et al., 2019; Sun et al., 2020a); and temporal models expose windows or event histories (Mei & Eisner, 2017; Yue et al., 2022; Xue et al., 2024b). The result is best read as lattice of permissible readouts rather than historical ladder: an encoder may expose compact global vector for first-stage search, local sequence or set for verification and grounding, discrete codes for reconstruction, and calibrated uncertainty for ambiguous items. Global vectors favor latency and storage; local or set-valued outputs favor correspondence and attribution; discrete objects favor rate-controlled generation (Défossez et al., 2023); distributions favor calibrated ambiguity (Chun et al., 2021). Evaluation should therefore report both the information an embedding preserves and the invariances it induces. The representational object and chosen granularity established here decide what can be aligned, fused, or reused in Sections 6 to 8: global vector, local set, code sequence, or distribution each 25 Omnimodal Embeddings exposes different cross-modal contract, and the three paths of Part III are each predicated on different assumption about which contract prevails. Takeaway The third axis of convergence is the upward shift of the representational object: every modality has moved from embedding the measurable atom (token, pixel, frame, sample) toward embedding whole semantic unit (sentence, image, utterance, series), driven by the same insightthe most directly comparable representation encodes whole, not its parts. The shift is not one-way ladder but bounded trade: pooling into coarser object buys invariance and efficient indexing yet discards the location, multiplicity, and correspondence some tasks need, so mature encoder exposes lattice of readouts and moves up or down it as the task demands. That lattice, not any single object, is what the alignment and fusion paths of Part III must operate on. 26 Omnimodal Embeddings

sections.title: 6 Path 1: Unification by Transformation
sections.content: We now trace the three-step progression toward omnimodal embeddings. Figure 5 sets the sharedbackbone case and the three paths side by side in single picture before we unpack them in turn: transformation (Section 6), alignment (Section 7), and joint fusion (Section 8), in order of increasing cross-modal interaction. To grade what each path actually achieves, we recall the 3C lens introduced in Section 1.4, which evaluates system by three progressively harder capabilities: coverage (C1: which modalities the system can ingest and test), comparability (C2: whether separately encoded modalities can be matched in shared metric space), and compositionality (C3: whether fused representation of multiple inputs genuinely depends on all of them rather than their simple sum). As we will see across Part III, the three paths satisfy these gates in turn. The first and most pragmatic path tries to unify modalities not by building new model but by transforming every modality into one that is already well-servedturning multimodal problem into single-modality one and reusing existing models. Transformation comes in three forms, each reuse of an existing, mature system: rendering non-visual data as images, serializing non-text data as text, and tokenizing continuous data into the discrete vocabularies that language models already consume. The first two leverage mature encoders trained on pixels and text; the third relies on the language-model interface itself. All are ingenious, and all suffer from information loss. Through the 3C lens, transformation primarily provides coverage: it lets an encoder trained on one modality accept another, but by itself guarantees neither comparability nor compositionalitywhich is why transforming modalities into one another so often loses the structure that the next two paths have to put back. 6.1 Rendering as Unifying Canvas The first transformation treats pixels as common computational medium: deterministic or learned renderer Rm maps an input xm to an image, after which visual backbone produces em = fvis(Rm(xm)). The appeal is obvious: it reuses the mature, heavily-pretrained image encoders and preserves the visual layout. But caveat is that comparability is not free: rendering confers shared shape, not shared semantics, and the renderer becomes part of the representation function. Rendering has been tried across an instructively wide range of modalities: Text image. PIXEL (Rust et al., 2023) renders sentences as images and performs masked-patch pretraining, replacing finite subword inventory with glyph-level visual input; CLIPPO (Tschannen et al., 2023) trains single ViT under contrastive objective over natural images and rendered text, extending the same pixel interface to imagetext retrieval and language tasks. (CLIPPO thereby straddles two paths: its interface is pure transformation, its objective is paired alignment. We group it throughout by its primary mechanism, as Figure 6 makes explicit.) Documents and screenshots image. The rendering familys most consequential success is where the modalitys semantics is visual layout: Pix2Struct pretrains on rendered web pages to parse screenshots (Lee et al., 2023); DSE directly embeds page screenshots as single dense vectors (Ma et al., 2024a); and ColPali shows that late-interaction retrieval over document images outperforms OCR-then-text pipelines on visually rich documents (Faysse et al., 2025). The LayoutLM line takes middle route by parsing the page first, and then injecting the recovered layout back into the token stream: two-dimensional positional embeddings over OCR tokens (Xu et al., 2020b), joined by the rendered image as an extra input channel in v2 (Xu et al., 2021b) and by unified textimage masking with wordpatch alignment in v3 (Huang et al., 2022c). Here rendering is not lossy approximation of text but the more faithful representation: 27 Omnimodal Embeddings Figure 5: Four ways of sharing work across modalities. The leading cell is the shared backbone (Section 4): one model serves every modality through modality-specific front ends, reusing parameters without necessarily producing shared representation space. The remaining three are the three bridges of Part III, in order of increasing cross-modal interaction: Transformation (Section 6) converts source item into target-form input before encoding, potentially losing or injecting information. Cross-modal alignment (Section 7) makes independently encoded representations comparable under shared metric. Joint fusion (Section 8) lets modalities interact before pooling, with optional inputs and private port retained, subsuming the alignment case (interaction set to zero). flat text serialization of document already discards the two-dimensional layout that carries its meaning. Text image, againbut for efficiency. 2025 line inverts PIXELs motivation: rather than rendering text for coverage, it renders text for compression. Glyph renders long contexts into images whose visual tokens are 34 fewer than the original text tokens (Cheng et al., 2026a), and DeepSeek-OCR pushes optical compression past 10 at usable OCR accuracy (Wei et al., 2025). Transformation, in this second guise, is no longer compromise made for an unserved modalityit is claim that the pixel channel is denser code for text than text tokens themselves. Graph image. GITA (Wei et al., 2024b) renders graph as drawing paired with textual description for vision-language graph reasoning. The strategy is clever but lossy: one drawing encodes graphs topology only as well as its labels and conventions allow, and the negative evidence is that multimodal LLMs still struggle with basic visual network analysis (Williams & Carley, 2024). Point cloud image. PointCLIP projects 3D point cloud into multi-view depth maps and feeds pretrained CLIP without any 3D pretraining (Zhang et al., 2022a)the transformation route by which the 3D point cloud family first reached shared-space model. Time series image. Gramian Angular Fields and Markov Transition Fields convert sequence into an image whose entries encode pairwise angular geometry or transition statistics before CNN processing (Wang & Oates, 2015); VisionTS recasts forecasting as image reconstruction 28 Omnimodal Embeddings and reuses visual masked autoencoder without any time-series pretraining (Chen et al., 2025c); and ViTST renders irregularly sampled series as line-chart images for ViT (Li et al., 2023h), the drawing conventions of the chart substituting for the interpolation numeric pipeline would have to invent. The successes and failures of rendering hinge on single question: whether two-dimensional projection preserves the structure the task actually queries. It works when the visual mapping captures the semantics that matter, such as glyph shapes of text or recurrence patterns of time series. And it excels in layout-bearing modalities: for documents, slides, web pages, and charts, the screenshot is not lossy projection of the semantics but is the semantics (Ma et al., 2024a; Faysse et al., 2025). Conversely, rendering fails when it flattens non-visual structure into pixels that vision encoder must awkwardly re-learn: 2D drawing can leave graphs edges implicit, and chart that rescales its axes discards the magnitude that time series treats as semantics (Lin et al., 2024). Rendering is unifying canvas, but canvas is 2D projection, and projection loses dimensionexcept when the modality already lived on the page. 6.2 Serialization as Unifying Language The second transformation leverages more mature ecosystem: it converts non-text data toward the text stack, either as strings that off-the-shelf text embedding or language models consume unchanged, or as continuous inputs that are projected directly into language models token embedding space. It is transformation that practitioners reach for first, because the text stacktokenizers, embedding models, rerankers, and retrieval APIsis the most engineered representation pipeline in existence. Time series string. Long before LLMs, SAX symbolized z-normalized, piecewiseaggregated window into word over small alphabet (Lin et al., 2007), and symbolic successors such as SAX-VSM (Senin & Malinchik, 2013) and BOSS (Schäfer, 2015) built classifiers and retrievers on the resulting words. The LLM era revived the same interface at scale: LLMTime shows that GPT-3, given string of number sequence, is competitive zero-shot forecaster, leveraging the unchanged next-token prior (Gruver et al., 2023); PromptCast recasts forecasting entirely as natural-language prompting (Xue & Salim, 2024); and TimeRAG retrieves numerical neighbors and injects them into the forecaster LLM as text prompts. LETS-C (Kaur et al., 2025) serializes each series for general text embedding model and fuses that embedding with the preprocessed numerical series by element-wise addition, outperforming 27 baselines on ten-dataset UEA benchmark. The headline is provocative but not clean control: either input alone trails the full model, so whether the text embedding itselfrather than the fused raw seriesmatches purpose-built architectures is question left open. Time series LLM embedding space. parallel stem bypasses the text interface and reuses the pretrained weights directly: TEST aligns series embeddings with text-prototype axes in frozen LLMs embedding space (Sun et al., 2024a), Time-LLM reprograms patched series into mixtures of the LLMs own word-embedding prototypes (Jin et al., 2024), GPT4TS/OFA lightly finetunes the positional embeddings and layer norms of frozen pretrained Transformer backbone for any time-series task (Zhou et al., 2023a), and aLLM4TS adapts LLM backbones via multi-patch prediction (Bian et al., 2024). Unlike the discrete tokenizers of Section 6.3, no member of this family introduces new time-series tokens: the LLMs sequence-processing weights are repurposed by directly accepting pseudo tokens of continuous patches. Graph text. Serializing graph is not one operation but design space: Talk like Graph shows that the choice of verbalizationnode list, edge list, adjacency, or incident description changes LLM performance by double digits (Fatemi et al., 2024); GraphText serializes node attributes and inter-node relationships by traversing graph-syntax tree (Zhao et al., 2023b); LLaGA organizes nodes into structure-aware sequences and projects their representations into the LLMs token embedding space (Chen et al., 2024d). The same lesson GITA taught by drawingone projection does not automatically preserve all of graphs topologyreappears here in linguistic form: which edges survive serialization is modeling decision, not property of the data. Omnimodal Embeddings Tables serialized schema and cells. For tables, the serialization-format sensitivity is welldocumented: TAPEX established that shared text decoder can execute SQL over linearized table (Liu et al., 2022a); TableLlama trains language model over serialized tables (Zhang et al., 2024c); and the Table meets LLM benchmark measures how markdown, JSON, and other formats alter LLM accuracy, finding none uniformly dominant (Sui et al., 2024). TableRAG embeds table by serializing its schema (column names, types, example values) and its cells (columnvalue pairs) with an off-the-shelf text encoder, then retrieves only the top-k fragments into the LM (Chen et al., 2024e). The approach makes million-token tables tractable, and is the clearest instance of transformation at work today. However, it is also cautionary tale: serialized column = value string has already discarded the rowcolumn geometry that structure-aware table encoders exist to preserve (Deng et al., 2020; Iida et al., 2021), so the transformation pays for scale with the very structure that made the table distinct modality. Non-text modalities text via cascade. The most common transformation in production systems is also the least discussed in the literature: transcribe, caption, then embed as text. Speech enters text embedder through ASR (Whispers outputs are embedded as if they were written language (Radford et al., 2023)), and images or videos enter through captioning (BLIPstyle captioners (Li et al., 2022a) feed text retriever in the default multimodal RAG pipeline). This cascade is text-as-hub in its most literal form: it works only to the extent that speech and vision are already verbalizable, and it fails, by construction, on content that never fits in wordsmusic, scene timbre, texture, and layout. Serialization is appealing because it is convenient and leverages the scaling advantages of LLMs, but it faces structural problem: string is 1D sequence, so whatever the modalitys native structure, the serialization must spell it out linearlyand the formats in wide use do not spell it all out, discarding the channel structure of multivariate series, the topology of graphs, the row column geometry of tables, and the magnitude that time series treats as semantics. Because symbolic pipelines rescale before discretizing (e.g., SAX z-normalizes (Lin et al., 2007), and Chronos applies mean scaling (Ansari et al., 2024)), 2C and 20C excursion of the same shape can map to the same symbols (Lin et al., 2024). The loss is not uniform, but most pronounced where the format leaves the native structure implicit, which is why tables and graphs suffer most under serialization while univariate forecasting suffers least. 6.3 Discrete Tokens: Leveraging the LM Interface The third transformation does not target text or pixels but the language models interface: learned codebook converts continuous data into streams of discrete tokens drawn from finite vocabulary the exact input shape that autoregressive models already consume. The codebook itselfreplacing continuous signal with its nearest entry in learned codebookis the classical idea of vector quantization, standard in image compression and signal coding long before deep learning (Gray, 1984), and revived later by VQ-VAE in vision (van den Oord et al., 2017); what is new here is the destination, which points the token stream at the LM interface. It is distinct in kind from the previous two transformations: serialization produces text verbatim and rendering produces pixels, but discrete token stream merely borrows the interfaceits words are invented by codec rather than attested in language. Audio codec tokens. Neural codecs (Zeghidour et al., 2022; Défossez et al., 2023) quantize waveform into stream of discrete tokens that an autoregressive model already consumes; this is how audio entered the language-model ecosystem. Distillation then organizes the token stream by information type, into semantic tokens carrying linguistic content and acoustic tokens carrying reconstruction detail: SpeechTokenizer distills HuBERTs latents into the first level of unified RVQ whose remaining levels recover the acoustic detail (Zhang et al., 2023b), RepCodec vector-quantizes pretrained speech representations directly into semantic tokens (Huang et al., 2024b), and Language-Codec redistributes information across fewer codebooks so that speech LMs consume fewer tokens (Ji et al., 2025). In the streaming setting, the Mimi codec of Moshi distills WavLM representations into semantic codebook alongside seven acoustic codebooks, 30 Omnimodal Embeddings giving real-time spoken-dialogue model one low-bandwidth token stream that separates content from acoustic detail (Défossez et al., 2024). Time series tokenized vocabularies. Chronos tokenizes series by scaling and rounding its values onto fixed integer vocabularytokens with no learned codebook at alland forecasts with language model over that vocabulary (Ansari et al., 2024); TOTEM learns modality-agnostic discrete codebook for series (Talukder et al., 2024), and byte-pair encoding over quantized values builds data-specific vocabulary (Götz et al., 2025). The advantage over serialization is that here the tokens can be learned where the structure is: codecs residual quantization can carry analog detail that string of digits or symbols flattens. But the strategy has boundary condition, and it is the same one the attested-unit argument will go on to sharpen (Section 9). Text and codec-tokenized speech have recurring unit inventorywords and phoneswhose identity is fixed by convention across corpora, which is why symbol system transfers for free: HuBERT works because audio has such an inventory (Hsu et al., 2021). modality without one is not barred from the step: tokenizer can manufacture an inventory of its own, and the payoff can followBEATs learned acoustic tokenizer supplies discrete labels that cluster same-content audio and drive masked prediction to state-of-the-art recognition (Chen et al., 2023c), and TOTEMs generalist time-series codebook outperforms per-domain specialists and transfers zero-shot to domains that share no sampling rate or sensor with its training corpus (Talukder et al., 2024). What manufactured vocabulary does not inherit is cross-corpus convention: because its tokens are defined per training set, whether they denote stable units across domains becomes an empirical precondition test that Section 10 formalizes as reuse rule. In summary, while transformation provides an immediate route to cross-modal coverage by borrowing mature text and vision pipelines, this convenience comes at the cost of structural lossflattening the very geometric or relational properties native to the source data. To preserve these native structures without lossy projections, the field turns to alignment, which leaves unimodal encoders intact and knits their coordinate spaces together. Takeaway Transformation is pragmatic shortcut that provides coverage at the expense of native geometry. Rendering preserves 2D layout but flattens magnitude and graph topology; serialization borrows LLM infrastructure but linearizes multidimensional relations; discretization enables LM sequence modeling but hinges strictly on recurring semantic units. When modalitys intrinsic semantics is visual layout (e.g., documents), transformation excels; elsewhere, its lossy projections expose exactly what genuine multimodal joint embedding must be engineered to preserve.

sections.title: 7 Path 2: Cross-Modal Alignment
sections.content: Transformation throws away information; the second path keeps each modalitys native encoder and stitches the resulting spaces together. This is the alignment paradigm that dominates cross-modal retrieval today: it achieves genuine semantic correspondence between modalities, and scales to many modalities without retraining everything pairwise via hub-and-spoke expansion. In the language of the 3C lens, alignment is the path that earns comparability, making separately encoded inputs mutually retrievable under shared metric. However, it hits dual ceiling that the next section will have to break: by construction, alignment cannot earn compositionality, since the two inputs never interact inside the model; and geometrically, aligned modalities still fail to occupy truly unified region in the space. 31 Omnimodal Embeddings 7.1 The Alignment Paradigm Dual towers plus contrastand its pre-web prehistory. The alignment recipe is architecturally simple: two (or more) independent encoders, one per modality, trained so that paired items map to nearby vectors and unpaired ones do not. The recipe is also old: DeViSE aligned visual embeddings into word-vector space with ranking loss back in 2013 (Frome et al., 2013), deep CCA optimized the same correspondence objective with learned nonlinear projections (Andrew et al., 2013), VSE++ showed that the crucial ingredient is hard negatives in the ranking loss (Faghri et al., 2018), and stacked cross attention (SCAN) added token-level interaction on top of aligned towers (Lee et al., 2018). On the audio side, SoundNet learned sound representations by transferring category structure from frozen visual classifier into an audio encoder (Aytar et al., 2016), and L3-Net (Arandjelovic & Zisserman, 2017) learned an audiovisual embedding from raw, unlabeled video by asking nothing more than whether frame and sound co-occurself-supervised correspondence in place of the paired web captions the recipe would later run on. What CLIP (Radford et al., 2021) changed was therefore neither the dual-tower architecture nor the contrastive loss (van den Oord et al., 2018) but the supervision corpus: natural-language supervision at web scale, with ALIGNs billion noisy pairs (Jia et al., 2021) turning well-established ranking objective into general-purpose representation learner. CLAP then ported the same recipe wholesale to audiolanguage (Elizalde et al., 2023; Wu et al., 2023b). The architecture is the dual-encoder of Section 4.3: each modality is encoded on its own, and comparison happens only in the shared space, which is what makes the resulting embeddings usable for efficient cross-modal nearest-neighbor retrieval at scale. This is why alignment, more than transformation, dominates production cross-modal retrieval: it preserves each modalitys strong native encoder while providing shared index. The web-scale family: losses, towers, and above all data. The recipe has since been refined along three axes that matter for what follows. In the loss, SigLIP replaces the softmax-normalized contrastive objective with pairwise sigmoid loss that does not normalize inside the batch (Zhai et al., 2023), decoupling quality from huge global batches and demonstrating robustness at essentially every scale; its successors extend this to multilingual and dense objectives (Tschannen et al., 2025; Xue & Xu, 2026). SigLIP towers are now the default visual front end of most open multimodal LLMsa quiet but consequential reuse that the convergence trend in Part II predicted. In the towers, LiT showed the image tower can be frozen while only the text encoder trains onto it (Zhai et al., 2022)the direct ancestor of the frozen-tower composition that jina-embeddings-v5-omni reprises (Section 7.3)and CoCa showed captioning head can be added so that one model serves both contrastive and generative consumers (Yu et al., 2022a). In the data, the decisive lever turned out to be curation rather than architecture: systematic studies of open-data scaling (Ilharco et al., 2021; Cherti et al., 2023), explicit curation of already-filtered pools (DataComp; Gadre et al., 2023), and end-to-end transparent filtering of the raw pool (MetaCLIP; Xu et al., 2024) each produced sizable gains that architectural tweaks did not, and EVA-CLIP pushed improved training techniques to the 18B-parameter regime (Sun et al., 2023a; 2024b). LLM2CLIP even shows the text tower can be replaced by an LLM that has seen no image but is only contrastively tuned on caption pairs (Huang et al., 2026b). The alignment paradigm, refined for four years, is thus the mature middle of the field, because its three dials (loss, towers, data) have all been optimized for web-scale regimes. The recipe ports to every pair. The strongest evidence that alignment is generalizable method rather than visionlanguage accident is how routinely the CLIP recipe has been transplanted. Video: CLIP4Clip adapted CLIPs towers with framewise pooling and temporal attention for text-tovideo retrieval (Luo et al., 2021), VideoCLIP pretrained videotext pairs directly (Xu et al., 2021a), and InternVideo2 scaled joint videotext pretraining to billion-parameter regimes (Wang et al., 2024f). Audio: LAION-CLAP (Wu et al., 2023b) and WavCaps (Mei et al., 2024) align general sound and caption embeddings, with WavCaps showing caption-like text can be manufactured (by ChatGPT) where it does not naturally occur. 3D: ULIP aligns point clouds to the CLIP imagetext space (Xue et al., 2023a), OpenShape scales 3D encoders toward open-world zero-shot recognition over natural-language descriptions (Liu et al., 2023b), and Uni3D scales the 3D encoder itself to billion parameters with reinstallation of visual and textual priors (Zhou et al., 2024c). Medicine: 32 Omnimodal Embeddings ConVIRT aligned radiology images with their reports (Zhang et al., 2022c), MedCLIP showed pairing can be learned from unpaired imagetext data (Wang et al., 2022d), BiomedCLIP scaled the recipe to the full biomedical literature (Zhang et al., 2023a), and CONCH pretrained pathology visionlanguage model on imagecaption pairs with joint contrastive and captioning objectives (Lu et al., 2023b). Molecules: MoleculeSTM aligns molecular graphs with natural language (Liu et al., 2023c), and CLAMP pretrains molecules contrastively against assay descriptions (Seidl et al., 2023). Time series: TS-CLIP aligns numerical time-series representations with textual captions under CLIP-shaped objective (Chen et al., 2025d)the most recent modality family to adopt this paradigm, and correspondingly the least settled. The pattern is this papers reuse axis made concrete: one objective, one training recipe, and one interface templatepaired data plus two towerstransplanted, unchanged in its essentials, to every modality family that could assemble paired corpus. What alignment buys. Alignment achieves true semantic correspondencesearching images with text, describing audio with languageand it does so while letting each modality keep its strongest encoder. It is the foundation on which every current cross-modal retrieval system is built, and the early omnimodal models such as e5-omni still lean on explicit cross-modal alignment to map text, image, video, and audio into one space (Chen et al., 2026b). 7.2 The Hub Choice: Which Modality Anchors the Space? Pairwise alignment does not scale combinatorially, and every multimodal system in this section therefore confronts the design axis that this subsection makes explicit: which modality should anchor the shared space? The anchor can play three distinct roles: hub modality that every spoke aligns to; coordinate system defined by fixed set of reference items rather than by any encoder at all; or frozen tower whose geometry new modalities are trained into rather than allowed to disturb. Binding into hub modality. That pretrained contrastive space can be extended with further modalities was demonstrated early on the audio side: AudioCLIP integrated third, audio tower into the CLIP imagetext space so that image, text, and audio embed into one geometry through joint contrastive training (Guzhov et al., 2022). ImageBind turned this one-off extension into general binding strategy, the hub-modality role: rather than aligning every modality to every other, it aligns each modality to single hub (image) using naturally available pairs (Girdhar et al., 2023). Because alignment to common anchor is approximately transitive, audio, depth, thermal, and text all end up in one shared space without ever being explicitly paired with one another. VIT-LENS generalizes this toward omnimodal representations through unified lens interface (Lei et al., 2024). The hub, however, is design axis, and the fields subsequent history can be read as debate over the choice of this anchor modality: LanguageBind answers text, aligning all modalities to the language tower (Zhu et al., 2024a); OmniBind goes pluralist, binding fourteen pretrained specialist spaces into one routed space (Wang et al., 2025c), with FreeBind showing the binding itself is cheap post-hoc operation on frozen encoders (Wang et al., 2024g); and C-MCR connects separately pretrained contrastive spacesnew modalities and new datasets alikeinto one shared space without retraining the underlying towers (Wang et al., 2023d). The trend of the past two years has been largely language-centric, for reason Section 1.2 prefigured: language is the only modality in which every other modality already has verbalized description, making natural pairs easily availableeven though it remains lossy hub that discards whatever was never put into words. Viewed through our analytical lens (Section 2.3), this hub-and-spoke paradigm neatly balances cross-modal intersection (a single shared anchor geometry) with modality-specific difference, as each spoke retains its own native encoder. Yet whichever hub is chosen, binding leaves residual offset between the towersthe geometric remainder that the methods of Section 7.3 explicitly set out to correct. Stitching: comparability retrofitted on frozen encoders. At the lightest end of this path sit methods that create comparability between encoders that are never retrained. Relative representations (Moschella et al., 2023) re-express every embedding by its similarity to fixed anchor set, 33 Omnimodal Embeddings making models trained on different datasets speak one coordinate system and merging them zeroshot; ASIF (Norelli et al., 2023) builds common multimodal space from unimodal models with nothing but paired data and similarity retrieval, updating in seconds. Both methods are trainingfree, and both define their coordinates through reference items rather than an encoder. Inside the network, model stitching asks the same question: can independently learned halves be reconnected? And it finds that well-trained representations routinely can, keeping both networks frozen while optimizing lightweight stitching layer on the tasks training set (Bansal et al., 2021). Conceptually, anchor-defined coordinates serve as the training-free counterpart of the hub-and-spoke architecture, where fixed set of reference items plays the role of hub modality encoder in ImageBind or LanguageBind, while stitching acts as their gradient-trained neighbor. The fact that either approach suffices to knit spaces together is itself compelling evidence for the latent shared geometry this paper leans on (Section 7.3). 7.3 The Limits of Alignment: The Modality Gap Alignments ceiling is striking geometric fact: even after training, the embeddings of different modalities do not occupy the same region of the shared space. Liang et al. (2022) named this the modality gap: in model like CLIP, image and text embeddings remain spatially segregated in two separate cones. This phenomenon persists across modalities (text, natural images, video, medical images, amino-acid sequences), and even manifests in models with random weights. Where the gap comes from. The modality gap has three-part origin (Liang et al., 2022). First, the cone effect: the inductive bias of deep networks with nonlinear activations shrinks the angle between any pair of embeddings, confining each encoders output to narrow cone (a phenomenon already seen in text anisotropy; Ethayarajh, 2019). Second, the two encoders of dual-tower model start from different random initializations and thus inhabit different cones from the startso the gap is present at initialization, before any data is seen. Third, the contrastive objective itself preserves the gap: under CLIPs default low temperature, the default gap distance is local minimum of the contrastive loss, so closing the gap increases the loss. The gap is therefore not an accident of architecture choice but joint consequence of initialization, activation geometry, and the contrastive losss temperature; this is why simply training longer does not remove it. Why it matters. The modality gap is direct obstacle to mixed-modality retrieval: query and candidate from different modalities sit in different cones, so nearest-neighbor search is biased, and the hubness problema few items absorbing disproportionate traffic, pathology intrinsic to high-dimensional spaces (Radovanovic et al., 2010) that worsens when vectors are mapped across spaces (Dinu & Baroni, 2015)is aggravated. Empirically, varying the gap distance alone changes CLIPs zero-shot accuracy and fairness (Liang et al., 2022), and balancing hub centrality remains an active retrieval concern (Bogolin et al., 2022; Faysse et al., 2025). Beyond three causes: what the gap is made of. The three-part diagnosis has since been refined in ways that matter for what alignment can be asked to do. Schrodi et al. (2024) find that only handful of embedding dimensions drive the gap, that both the gap and CLIPs object bias trace back to single triggerthe information imbalance between an image and its captionand that the gap modulates the entropy of the models logits, carrying functional load rather than being pure pathology. The C3 recipe (Connect, Collapse, Corrupt) tests the constructive side: it deliberately collapses the gap to make text embeddings interchangeable with image embeddings, enabling crossmodal captioning and generation from unimodal data alone (Zhang et al., 2024e). And GR-CLIP shows the pragmatic side: for mixed-modality search where corpus mixes text-only, image-only, and multimodal documents, the gap is ranking pathology, and training-free post-hoc centering of each modalitys embeddings improves NDCG@10 by up to 26 points over CLIP (Li et al., 2026a). final refinement reaches past the geometry of the gap to what its zero-shot tests can even mean: whether an aligned space retrieves concept zero-shot at all is largely set by the concepts frequency in the web-scale pretraining corpus, with performance decaying steeply over the long tail of rare Omnimodal Embeddings concepts (Udandarao et al., 2024). Taken together, these results temper the gap narrative in both directions. On one hand, the gap is more than surface artifact, as few dimensions carry systematic modality information retrieval stack must handle. On the other hand, it is less damning than it appears, since whether it hurts depends on the tasks modality mixturea nuisance to be removed in mixed-modality search, functionally loaded structure to be respected in unimodal zero-shot classification, and an obstacle to be collapsed when embeddings must be interchangeable. Mitigation, and deeper convergence. Recent work closes the gap from two angles. I0T standardizes aligned embeddings to push toward zero modality gap (An et al., 2025); jina-embeddings-v5omni preserves text geometry while adding modalities through locked aligned towers (Hönicke et al., 2026). More fundamentally, Jha et al. (2025) show that universal latent geometry underlies different embedding spaces, enabling unsupervised translation of embeddings from one vector space to another without paired dataevidence that the gap is coordinate artifact superimposed on representation that is, at deeper level, already aligned, though the demonstration is so far strongest between text embedding spaces and covers only small number of cross-modal model pairs (Jha et al., 2025). The training-free comparability results above (Moschella et al., 2023; Norelli et al., 2023; Li et al., 2026a) are what the hypothesis needs next: converging witnesses, partial, but independent of any single model pair. The hypothesis is the Platonic Representation Hypothesis (Huh et al., 2024) made operational: if shared geometry exists beneath the cones, the gap is surface phenomenon, and the right architecture would expose the shared geometry directly rather than aligning two separate cones. Alignment is still relevant in the MLLM era. One might expect the alignment paradigm to have been obsoleted by single-stream multimodal LLMs, yet the 202526 SOTA says otherwise. Qwen3VL-Embeddings retrieval stack keeps an indexable bi-encoder embedding model paired with, but separate from, an explicit cross-encoder reranker (Li et al., 2026b). jina-embeddings-v5-omni builds its omni space by locking frozen text tower and aligning new modality towers onto its geometry (Hönicke et al., 2026). Most strikingly, Omni-Embed-Nemotron reports that for audio video retrieval, encoding the two streams separatelywithout the token-level interleaving that generative omni models use for synchronized understandingoutperforms the interleaved fusion of its own backbone (Xu et al., 2025a). And LCO-Emb argues the deeper reason: latent cross-modal alignment is already present inside MLLMs as by-product of generative pretraining, so contrastive tuning is refinement of an existing alignment rather than the creation of one (Xiao et al., 2025a). The boundary between alignment and fusion is thus blurring into question of where inside the pipeline modality-specific streams meetbut the design lesson survives: indexable, separately encoded modalities remain the anchor of most deployed retrieval systems, which is why the next path must treat alignment as something to subsume, not abolish. Takeaway Alignment is the pragmatic path that earns comparability: it stitches independently encoded modalities into shared retrieval index at scale without pairwise retraining. Yet it hits fundamental ceiling. Contrastive dual encoders inevitably leave modalities segregated in separate conesa persistent modality gap driven by initialization and informational asymmetry. Because inputs are related only by contrastive pairs rather than joint computation, alignment coordinates spaces without forming truly unified semantic object, falling inherently short of compositionality and necessitating deep joint fusion.

sections.title: 8 Path 3: Multimodal Joint Embedding
sections.content: Transformation shares representation by flattening modalities into one. Alignment shares an index but keeps encoders separate. The third path, our advocated terminus, fuses modalities by letting them interact inside the model, producing single joint representation that encodes their interaction 35 Omnimodal Embeddings rather than merely the proximity of separately encoded parts. This section describes the fusion paradigm, makes the central positional argument of the paperjoint embedding is more general framework that unifies and surpasses alignmentand then distills the desiderata good multimodal joint embedding model must satisfy. In the language of the 3C lens, fusion is the path that targets compositionality: genuinely joint vector should depend on all its inputs and cannot be reproduced by adding separately encoded ones. Picking up the picture of Figure 5, the rest of this section makes the case that fusion subsumes alignment as strict generalization, making it the terminus of the three-step progression. Table 5 then catalogs the degrees of fusion in between mere score combination and full token-level interaction, mapping each to representative systems. 8.1 The Fusion Paradigm Which streams attend to which: two kinds of fusion. The literature labels both of the following (A) Intra-item fusion: the streams being fused are the as fusion, and they must be kept apart. modalities of one iteman imagetext pair that constitutes query, videoaudio document that constitutes candidateand the output is single embedding of that item. This is what VLM2Vec, GME, MM-Embed, and the omni-embedders of this section do; it remains bi-encoder over items, so items can still be encoded and indexed offline. (B) Querycandidate cross-encoding: the streams being fused are the query and the candidate themselvesa reranker that feeds both through one modelproducing reranking score only and no embedding of the item at all. The two share the mechanics of cross-attention but not the economics: (A) keeps offline indexability at the price of heavier encoder, while (B) forfeits it and pays forward pass per (query, candidate) pair. In this paper, joint embedding always refers to (A), as (B) produces pairwise scores rather than indexable representations; we revisit (B) briefly at the end of this subsection only to acknowledge that deployed stacks routinely pair both. From visionlanguage pretraining to fusion. The fusion paradigm predates MLLMs. Early vision language pretraining explored both multi-stream architectures, which process the two modalities in separate streams that meet in co-attention layers (Lu et al., 2019; Tan & Bansal, 2019), and single-stream architectures that build one Transformer over concatenated visual and textual token streams (Chen et al., 2020d; Kim et al., 2021), with FLAVA and BEiT-3 later unifying image, text, and imagetext objectives at scale (Singh et al., 2022; Wang et al., 2022b). Pretraining objectives varied across these modelsmasked multimodal modeling and alignment prediction in ViLBERT, LXMERTs five tasks from masked language modeling to cross-modality matching and image question answeringwith the matching heads taking the regime-B cross-encoder form of interaction. The pairing that would become standarda dual-encoder imagetext contrastive (ITC) head plus an imagetext matching (ITM) cross-encoder headwas crystallized by ALBEF, whose recipe is literally align before fuse: the ITC loss acts on unimodal representations before fusion, jointly optimized with ITM and masked language modeling (Li et al., 2021); BLIP bootstraps both from synthetic captions (Li et al., 2022a), and BLIP-2 projects the Q-Formers output query embeddings into the input space of frozen language model as soft visual prompts (Li et al., 2023d)the hand-off that produced the MLLM embedders below. The design of that hand-off has since come under audit: DeCo argues that compressive projectors such as the QFormer abstract the visual stream prematurely, and that compressing patch tokens while leaving semantic abstraction to the decoder is both cheaper and better (Yao et al., 2024), while Cross-Layer Injection replaces the single static connection with dynamic bridge through which the decoder draws on every vision layer on demand (Chen et al., 2026a). This early pretraining era is thus, in retrospect, where the field discovered that alignment and interaction are two operating modes of one architecturea discovery central to Section 8.2. In audiovisual learning the same arc runs from VATT (Akbari et al., 2021) to attention bottlenecks, which show that restricting cross-modal attention to few tokens both regularizes and improves fusion (Nagrani et al., 2021). Cross-attention as deep interaction. Where alignment uses an independent dual-encoder, intraitem fusion uses cross-attention: queries from one modality attend to keys and values from another, so that each modalitys representation is conditioned on the others content. Recall from Section 4.1 36 Omnimodal Embeddings Table 5: Ways to combine inputs, ordered by how early and at what resolution the inputs interact. Letting inputs interact earlier and at finer resolution can preserve more detail, but leaves less computation to cache. The examples map fusion mechanisms to representative systems: the deeper the interaction, the more capability shifts from comparability toward compositionality. Mechanism Construction Representative system Strength Main trade-off Score fusion = wmsm Late-fusion rerankers; UniIR score-fusion variants (Wei et al., 2024a) Reuses unimodal indices; handles missing inputs Vector fusion = norm(m wmem) Additive cross-modal baselines Learned composition = h(e1, . . . , ek, r) Pseudo-token composition Translate one modality into another token space Token/feature fusion = pool(F(H1:k, r)) Multi-part output Global local/input-specific components plus TIRG (Vo et al., 2019) (gated composition of global image and text features) VISTA (Zhou et al., 2024b) (visual tokens injected into text encoder) Everything at Once (Shvetsova et al., 2022), VLM2Vec (Jiang et al., 2025), UniIR featurefusion variants (Wei et al., 2024a), LCO-Embedding (Xiao et al., 2025a), MM-Embed (Lin et al., 2025) Multi-vector / late-interaction retrieval (Faysse et al., 2025) Low-cost, cacheable, modular Models interactions among input vectors at low cost Reuses pretrained models ability to combine tokens May not produce combined embedding Fixed addition cannot model correspondence or conflict Compresses local evidence before interaction Loses information the target token space cannot express Models fine-grained before interaction pooling Requires re-encoding; cost grows with tokens Supports retrieval, attribution and fallback More complex storage, APIs and evaluation that self-attention is permutation-equivariant all-to-all operator; cross-attention is its bipartite counterpart, universal relational operator between two token sets. Where contrastive alignment learns only that pair corresponds, fusion learns how they correspondwhich parts of caption describe which regions of an image, which audio moment matches which frame (Shvetsova et al., 2022). For symmetric multimodal-to-multimodal retrieval, SOLAR learns an intersection mask over each fused imagetext pair so that one joint vector keeps both the shared semantics and the complementary difference, showing that the interaction can reach into the construction of the embedding itself (Yang et al., 2026). The interaction is not free: attention is quadratic in the token counts of the streams being combined, so fused encoders are strictly more expensive than their separately encoded partsbut the encoding stays per item and therefore remains pre-computable. From fusion to omnimodal embedders. The fusion paradigm is now driving wave of multimodal embedding models that treat embedding as first-class output of fused model rather than the byproduct of two aligned towers. The wave began from the text side: VISTA injects visual token embeddings into pretrained text embedder so that single global vector serves text, image, and imagetext items alike (Zhou et al., 2024b). VLM2Vec trains vision-language models for massive multimodal embedding tasks, conditioning the representation on instruction (Jiang et al., 2025); its successor extends coverage to video and visual documents with the MMEB-V2 benchmark (Meng et al., 2026). Everything at Once fuses audio, video, and text for video retrieval through multimodal fusion transformer (Shvetsova et al., 2022). cluster of universal multimodal retrievers MM-Embed (Lin et al., 2025), GME (Zhang et al., 2025c), UniME (Gu et al., 2025) and its judgeaugmented successor (Gu et al., 2026), and the Douyin Multimodal Embedding model (Chen et al., 2026c)train MLLMs to produce fused embeddings across text, image, and beyond, using instruction tuning, modality-aware hard negatives, and synthetic multimodal data. The pace of refinement is rapid and the levers refined are familiar: high-quality synthetic data in mmE5 (Chen et al., 2025a), hardness-weighted contrastive samples in LLaVE (Lan et al., 2025a), and bidirectional attention restored to decoder backbone via modality-aware continual pretraining in MoCa (Chen et al., 2026d), whose main lesson is that the causal masked MLLM is rarely the best encoder without such repair. LamRA frames the whole stack as one system, coupling an embedder and companion reranker as separate LoRA modules over one MLLMwith the reranker trained on hard negatives 37 Omnimodal Embeddings mined by the embedder (Liu et al., 2025b); MegaPairs pushes the data side, synthesizing massive (query, positive, hard negative) triplets over one MLLM for universal multimodal retrieval (Zhou et al., 2025b). Most striking is E5-V: finetuned on text pairs only, it generalizes to image and interleaved retrieval, and even to an imageimage retrieval suite in which the queries are captions rendered as images (Jiang et al., 2024b)together with LCO-Embs demonstration that latent alignment is by-product of generative pretraining (Xiao et al., 2025a), the strongest evidence to date that the alignment the previous path works to build already exists latently inside the MLLM, waiting to be read out. And the omnimodal frontierQwen3-VL-Embedding with its reranking-distilled bi-encoder embedder and Matryoshka dimensions (Li et al., 2026b), e5-omni combining explicit cross-modal alignment with fusion (Chen et al., 2026b), language-centric omni pretraining showing that continual generation before contrastive fusion raises the representation ceiling (Xiao et al., 2025a; Yoo et al., 2026), WAVE for general audiovisual correspondence (Tang et al., 2026), OmniEmbed-Nemotron with deliberately non-interleaved audio and video streams (Xu et al., 2025a), and Ovis-Embedding as the leading MMEB-V3 system at review time (Team, 2026)now targets all of text, image, video, and audio in single encoder rather than an aligned set of towers. Fusion, in short, is no longer specialized architecture for particular cross-modal task; it is becoming the default way to build multimodal embedding. Reasoning and generative embedding. The newest fork of this path pushes the representation generation unification of Section 3 to its logical end: let the model reason before it embeds. ThinkThen-Embed precedes the embedding readout with short generated rationale, and shows the rationales text improves multimodal retrieval (Cui et al., 2026); UME-R1 trains embedding generation with reinforcement learning over retrieval rewards, arguing generative embeddings (LLM tokens used directly as embeddings) benefit more from reasoning than discriminative ones (Lan et al., 2025b); Retrv-R1 balances reasoning gains against latency costs with thinking-mode schedules (Zhu et al., 2025); and VladVA shows general LVLM can simply be discriminatively finetuned into competitive (M)EB-style embedder (Ouali et al., 2025). The text-side analogs are already numerous (Muennighoff et al., 2025; Yan et al., 2026; Chen et al., 2026e), which suggests this is not transient modality-specific trend but the objective layer of Section 3 finally reaching the multimodal sideand, in UME-R1s generative embedding, genuinely new answer to what the representational object of an embedding model can be. Composed and multi-vector readouts. Where compositionality is the task rather than the architecture, fusion shows up as composed retrieval, whose query is itself an input paira prior image plus modification instruction: TIRG composed such queries within Siamese network (Vo et al., 2019), with benchmark families CIRR and FashionIQ (Liu et al., 2021; Wu et al., 2021) operationalizing the task; Pic2Word and SEARLE learn textual inversionmapping images into the word-embedding space of frozen CLIPso the composed query is embeddable without retraining CLIP itself (Saito et al., 2023; Baldrati et al., 2023); MagicLens self-supervises (query image, instruction, target image) triplets from web pairs and shows dual-encoder suffices for open-ended instructions, far beyond the classic modification text (Zhang et al., 2024b); CoVR ported the recipe to video (Ventura et al., 2024). Where the readout is the object, multi-vector and late-interaction formatsColPali over document patches (Faysse et al., 2025), Matryoshka nested dimensions (Kusupati et al., 2022), jinaembeddings-v4s task-conditioned training and multi-vector modes (Günther et al., 2025)populate the multi-part row of Table 5, with MetaEmbed making the number of interaction vectors test-time dial on single late-interaction model (Xiao et al., 2026), turning the lattice of readouts of Section 5 from training-time commitment into an inference-time budget. Beyond embedding: reranking as full fusion (regime B). For completeness, the querycandidate regime is the classical cross-encoderthe same dual-encoder/cross-encoder split that the reranking literature formalized for text (Zhuang et al., 2023)and it is thriving in the multimodal stack precisely because it buys the accuracy that precomputable embedding must leave behind: Qwen3VL-Reranker is the companion cross-encoder trained alongside Qwen3-VL-Embedding (Li et al., 2026b), and MM-R5 brings reinforcement learning to multimodal reasoning reranker (Xu et al., 2025b). Rerankers produce no reusable representationeach (query, candidate) pair is re-scored 38 Omnimodal Embeddings from scratchand are therefore consumers of embeddings rather than producers. Their practical importance is that the strongest omnimodal retrieval systems are (A)+(B) pipelines, with an indexable intra-item-fusion embedding first and cross-encoder reranker over its top-k (Liu et al., 2025b; Li et al., 2026b). 8.2 Joint Embedding as General and Ultimate Framework We now make the argument that elevates fusion from one path among three to the terminus of the journey. The core insight: fusion subsumes alignment. The key observation is that joint-embedding (fusion) model is strict generalization of an alignment model. dual-encoder alignment model is simply joint-embedding model in which the cross-modal interaction has been set to zero an architecture that fuses nothing and falls back to comparing independently encoded vectors. Conversely, exposing the interaction (cross-attention) can only add information the alignment model lacks: the relative arrangement of tokens across modalities that no contrastive pair can capture. The vision-language pretraining era supplies the cleanest architectural witness: ALBEF and BLIP carried both regimes on one backbonean imagetext contrastive (alignment) head and an imagetext matching (interaction) headand the interaction side won precisely on the tasks where correspondence matters (Li et al., 2021; 2022a), so interaction behaves as dial on one architecture rather than separate paradigm. This is the compositional gain argument, which Section 11 makes operational as measurable criterion (comp): genuinely joint vector should beat the strongest unimodal encoder and the additive baselines of score fusion and vector addition (Jiang et al., 2025), because it captures cross-modal interactions the others cannot. Partial information decomposition gives the claim its motivation: the information that multiple inputs carry about target decomposes into redundant, unique, and synergistic parts (Liang et al., 2023a), of which only the synergistic part is absent from every single input, emerging solely from the joint variable. comp operationalizes this requirement (with its empirical caveats detailed in Section 11). By this logic we conjecture that in the capacity-unconstrained limit, fusion weakly dominates alignmentthere would be no regime in which the architecture is at principled disadvantage, only regimes in which fusions interaction term is unnecessary and its compute cost is wasted, in which case the two coincide. The limit is also where the conjecture must stop: capacity, data mixture, and modality imbalance each break it in practice (Zhang et al., 2025d; Lin et al., 2025; Li et al., 2026b; Huang et al., 2026a), and Omni-EmbedNemotron finds that interleaved audiovideo fusion can underperform separately encoded streams using the same backbone on audiovideo retrieval (Xu et al., 2025a). Whether fusions extra capacity pays off at given compute and data budget is therefore an empirical question, and is what the C3 compositional-gain controls of Section 11 are designed to test. One model, two operating modes. This generalization yields striking consequence. single joint-embedding model has two operating modes determined by the input: Multimodal in fusion. When the input spans modalities, the streams interactthrough explicit cross-attention, or through the shared self-attention of single-stream backbone over concatenated tokensand the model is fusion model, producing representation of the interaction. Unimodal in stronger single-/cross-modal model. When only one modality is presented, single-stream backbones degrade gracefully to within-modality attention, the other tokens being simply absent; explicit cross-attention designs instead need defined policy for the missing stream, such as skipping or substituting its keys and values. Under either design the same parameters can serve as strong encoder for the lone modalityone that, having been trained on cross-modal interaction, benefits from the auxiliary signal and richer supervision. The same parameters serve both regimes, and in the limit the model would forfeit no capability by being general. This is the operational reading of the Platonic convergence (Huh et al., 2024) and the universal-geometry result (Jha et al., 2025): if single geometry underlies all modalities, 39 Omnimodal Embeddings single model trained to expose it should be at least as good on any one modality as specialist, and strictly better on their combination. E5-Vs text-only training is this prediction run in reverse: finetuned on text pairs alone, the model transfers to image and composed-image retrieval (Jiang et al., 2024b). At finite capacity the transfer is, however, not automatic: counterexamples such as Qwen3-VL-Embedding (Zhang et al., 2025d; Li et al., 2026b) and MM-Embed (Lin et al., 2025) show that joint multimodal training can leave the encoder worse than matched specialist on single modality, so matching the specialist is not property fusion inherits for free, but constraint the training recipe must actively enforcethrough data mixture, remediation stages, or distillation back to the specialist. Why this is the terminus. The three paths are therefore not three parallel options but progression. Transformation serves as coarse first approximation by homogenizing inputs at the cost of structural loss; alignment provides mature compromise through shared metric spaces, though constrained by persistent modality gaps; and joint embedding represents the terminus, unifying representations through deep interaction, fusing when it can and specializing when it must. The reason alignment cannot be the endpoint is the modality gap of Section 7.3; the reason joint embedding can be is that it removes the two-cone structure at its source, computing within rather than acrossa removal that must be driven by the right prompts and objectives, since shared encoder alone still leaves clear gap (Jiang et al., 2024b). The reason transformation cannot compete is information loss; the reason joint embedding avoids it is that the modality-specific structure (the things transformation discards) survives inside the fused representation and can be attended to where relevant. The terminus, notably, is not an engineering convenience alone: it is where this road map meets the architecture the brain uses for concepts, as argued in Section 1.2. Human semantic memory is organized hub-and-spokeone modality-invariant convergence zone (Damasio, 1989) carrying concepts across all modalities, flanked by modality-specific spokes (Patterson et al., 2007)and multisensory cues are fused within single reliability-weighted computation (Ernst & Banks, 2002): an arrangement that pairwise comparison cannot express but joint embedding instantiates. Caveats and open costs. Two honest caveats frame Part IV. First, fusion is expensive: intra-item cross-attention is quadratic in the interacting token counts, which is why late-interaction and Matryoshka-style approximations remain an active research area (Kusupati et al., 2022; Faysse et al., 2025; Xiao et al., 2026). Second, naive fusion is not free of pathologies: modality collapsein which the generative decoder reconstructs one modality and ignores anotheris documented failure mode of multimodal latent-variable models (Javaloy et al., 2022); on-the-fly gradient modulation exists because one modalitys gradients can suppress anothers during joint training (Peng et al., 2022); and modality competition identifies provable regimes in which joint training is worse than single-modality training on every constituent modality (Huang et al., 2022b) and asks what makes joint training help (Huang et al., 2021b). Information-bottleneck analyses sharpen the same warning from another side. Contrastive losses are built to preserve what the modalities share: they neither remove modality-specific nuisance (Almudévar et al., 2025), nor protect modality-specific signal the unique (not just synergistic) component that partial information decomposition formalizes (Liang et al., 2023a;b). MM-Embeds documented modality biasjoint training on interleaved multimodal inputs degrading its text retrieval until dedicated remediation stage restores it (Lin et al., 2025) is the production symptom of this family of pathologies. Building joint embedding that truly fuses without collapsing is an open problemone whose shape the desiderata of Section 8.3 make concrete, and that, as the next chapters argue, requires respecting what is modality-specific rather than dismissing or overlooking it. 8.3 Desiderata for Multimodal Joint Embedding Model If joint embedding is to be the terminus, progress toward it needs definition: what separates good joint embedding model from merely fused one? The evidence assembled in this chapterthe collapse pathologies of joint training and the remediation stages that answer them, the capacity limits that keep the transfer between the two operating modes from being automaticalready points to compact set of design criteria. Stating them explicitly serves two purposes at once: it turns the 40 Omnimodal Embeddings framework argued above into checklist any claimed joint embedding can be held to, and it gives Section 11 properties to test. We state five. Preserve each modalitys own interface and parameters. Fusion is not license to homogenize the periphery. Modality-specific tokenizers are the interface through which modality structure enters the model (Section 4.1), and the same argument reaches the backbone parameters: when every feed-forward pathway is fully shared, the modalities demands average into lowest common denominatorthe same regime the caveats above identify as modality competition (Huang et al., 2022b). The architectural answer is to accommodate modality specialization through dedicated capacity rather than allowing it to bottleneck shared parameters: VLMos Mixture-ofModality-Experts keeps shared self-attention layer over pools of modality-specific experts and, tellingly, is trained stagewiseits shared attention and vision expert are pretrained on image-only data, then frozen while the language expert trains alone on text, and only then does the model meet imagetext pairs (Bao et al., 2022b); MoE-LLaVA sustains visual understanding at constant inference cost through sparsely activated experts (Lin et al., 2026). The criterion has both mechanistic and an information-theoretic face: undifferentiated mixing is what triggers the collapse and gradient-interference pathologies discussed above, and the modality-unique component of the decomposition is what fully shared trunk has no route to preserve (Liang et al., 2023a). Let each modality deepen before it meets the others. Fusion should be late-stage act. layerwise analysis finds that fused models defer most cross-modal token interaction to middle and deeper layersso much so that multimodal tokens can bypass the early layers of the language backbone with little or no loss (Choraria et al., 2026)and the training recipes that work follow the same schedule from the other side: the audio-language line raises its ceiling through continual generation before contrastive alignment (Xiao et al., 2025a; Yoo et al., 2026), e5-omni couples an explicit cross-modal alignment stage with fusion (Chen et al., 2026b), and VLMos stagewise pretraining above is the visionlanguage instance of the same schedule (Bao et al., 2022b). The reading is that early, undifferentiated mixing creates the very collapse surfaces the first criterion warns against: once shallow layers have averaged what the streams carry, deeper layers cannot tell the modalities apart again. Fuse for composition, not consensus. The point of joint embedding is the interaction term, so the model must be optimized and held to it. As noted in Section 8.2, contrastive losses hold the model only to what the modalities sharethe task-relevant content unique to single modality is not protected, and modality-specific nuisance is not removed (Almudévar et al., 2025; Liang et al., 2023b)which is acceptable for alignment but insufficient here, where capturing the synergistic component (Section 8.2; Liang et al., 2023a) is the whole point. The criterion is therefore measurable: joint model earns its name only where it beats the strongest unimodal encoder and the additive baselines, which is the compositional gain comp detailed in Section 11. Audit the unimodal mode; do not assume it. joint model lives in the two operating modes of Section 8.2, and the criterion is that unimodal performance must not quietly degrade: the production counterexamples aboveMM-Embeds dedicated remediation stage, Qwen3-VLEmbedding falling short of matched specialistsshow that parity with specialists must be enforced by the recipe through data mixture, curriculum, remediation, or distillation (Huang et al., 2022b). Treat absent streams and flexible readouts as first-class. deployed omni-encoder sees every subset of the modalitiestext-only queries against imagetext candidates, streams that arrive late or not at allso the design must define its policy for missing stream rather than let one emerge, and expose readouts at more than one granularity, since cross-modal tasks differ in whether they want one vector, set, or reranking score (Section 5). That such interface policies have retrieval consequences is an experimental fact, as Omni-Embed-Nemotrons non-interleaved audiovideo design demonstrated in Section 8.2. The five criteria compound: the first two say where modality-specific structure should live (the periphery, the early depth), the last three say what the fusion itself must deliver (composition, 41 Omnimodal Embeddings parity, robustness), and all five are testablemaking them the natural complement to the 3C lens operationalized in Section 11. From mechanism to trajectory. Figure 5 opened Part III by abstracting the three bridge mechanisms in isolation; Figure 6 closes it by situating those mechanisms against the per-modality histories that produced themfrom modality-specific foundations, through the transformation and alignment bridges, to the joint-fusion models and the three 3C requirements they must ultimately answer. Where Figure 5 fixed the mechanisms, Figure 6 fixes the milestones: taken together they frame the progression we argue the field is in the middle of, from separate encoders to single fusion model that inherits them all. Takeaway Joint embedding unifies and surpasses alignment. It is the omnimodal embedding model in its ultimate form: single encoder whose representational object is the joint semantics of whatever modalities it is given, that reduces to strong specialist when given single modalitya level that, at finite capacity, the training recipe must actively maintainand that closes the modality gap at its source when paired with appropriate objectives and prompting. Reaching this end, however, demands that we stop ignoring modality-specific structure and instead learn to preserve and even borrow itthe subject of Part IV. 42 i a b i s 4 3 Figure 6: From modality-specific foundations to omnimodal embedding. Left: ten modality families each climb the same four-era ladder hand-crafted units, deep supervised/contextual encoders, self-supervised and contrastive pretraining, and foundation-scale or LLM-native encoderswhich is the per-modality face of the convergence argued in Part II. Middle: shared backbone (Section 4) and the three Part III bridges, ordered by interaction depth: transformation (Section 6) converts inputs into format an existing encoder already serves; alignment (Section 7) keeps separate towers and learns shared metric; joint fusion (Section 8) lets inputs interact before pooling. Right: the 3C lens with representative instruments for each capability (Section 11). Solid arrows mark the capability mechanism most directly supports; dashed arrows mark secondary support. Groupings indicate the primary mechanism, not an exclusive class. Omnimodal Embeddings

sections.title: 9 Frontier I: Mastering Modality-Specific Properties
sections.content: To build joint embedding that truly fuses rather than collapses, we must first respect what is modality-specificthe difference axis of our analytical lens. The convergence of Part II tells us the encoders and objectives can be shared; the difference axis tells us what each modality demands the shared machinery preserve or invent. joint embedding model that ignores these properties discards the very information that made each modality worth encoding. This chapter inventories the defining difficulty of each modality and the methods it has forced into being. Table 6 frames the inventory as practical input taxonomy: for each family, which structure must be preserved and the representative evidence, tagged by whether the input is raw observation, derived view, structured view, or compound format. Text and code: discreteness and compositionality. Text is inherently discretea finite vocabulary composed by syntaxand its semantics are compositional. This is both an enabler and burden. Discreteness makes text amenable to tokenization and gives it an attested, recurring unit inventory (words, subwords), which is why MLM, contrastive disambiguation, and skip-gram-style objectives all work (Mikolov et al., 2013; Devlin et al., 2019; Gao et al., 2021). But compositionality breeds massive polysemybank denotes financial institution, river edge, or verband the contextual representations that must resolve it tend to be anisotropic, collapsing into narrow cone (Ethayarajh, 2019); contrastive finetuning is in part mechanism for disambiguating the embedding space. Code is text but not just text: it adds executable semantics (two functions may be syntactically dissimilar but semantically equivalent (Huang et al., 2024a)) and cross-language equivalence (implementations of an algorithm in Python and Java share semantics despite divergent lexicon (Utpala et al., 2024)), and it carries hierarchical structuretokens, expressions, statements, functions, modules, projectsthat current models flatten rather than exploit (Jin et al., 2023a; Li et al., 2025b). The codeencoders own history shows how these layers were reclaimed one at timesurface tokens (Feng et al., 2020), AST syntax, data-flow semantics (Guo et al., 2021)and the compilers intermediate representation (IR) marks the current frontier of that process: the IR is already machine-oriented normalization of behavior, so IR-based embeddings are languageand machine-independent by construction (VenkataKeerthy et al., 2020), and have been shown to benefit downstream applications such as clone detection (Li et al., 2022c)evidence that compiler-transformed views are productive axis of invariance joint embedding can declare. joint embedding must capture compositional meaning without losing disambiguation, and must learn to represent codes behavioral equivalence, not just its surface form. Vision: spatial topology and multi-scale composition. Vision has no canonical counterpart to word2vec: pixel at coordinate (i, j) is not the same entity across images, patch boundaries are imposed by preprocessing, and object identity must be inferred across scale, viewpoint, deformation, and occlusion. Continuity is not the obstacle; choosing stable recurring units and meaningful context relation across scenes and resolutions is (Sivic & Zisserman, 2003; van den Oord et al., 2017). Visual semantics are spatial, compositional, and multi-scale: edges compose into textures and objects, and the same entity produces different measurements under translation, illumination, and occlusion, while multiple entities coexist in one frame. The representation must therefore choose between invariance (recognition may discard position and texture) and equivariance (correspondence, geometry, and generation require them) (Long et al., 2015; Caron et al., 2021). Video adds temporal axis and hierarchy of units (frame, clip, track, event), so strong image encoder is necessary appearance model but not complete video representationmotion must be retained where retrieval is motion-sensitive (Tong et al., 2022; Devaraj et al., 2024). joint embedding must preserve this spatial and temporal correspondence, not collapse scene to single global point. 44 Omnimodal Embeddings Table 6: practical input taxonomy for the modality-specific challenges of Section 9. denotes raw observation, derived view, structured view, and compound format. Tensor shape does not define modality: RGB and thermal are both arrays but measure different quantities. domain label such as medical is not itself modality. Family Examples and type Structure to preserve Representative evidence Language and symbols Natural language and code (R); tables and markup (S) Discrete sequence, hierarchy and references; code adds syntax, flow and execution Visible and dynamic vision RGB image, video and event streams (R);
