flow, segmentation, keypoints and boxes (D) 2D topology; video/events add order, rate, sparse time and motion Geometry and 3D Depth, LiDAR (R/D); point sets, meshes, voxels, poses and fields (S/D) Metric coordinates, surface topology and SE(3) behavior Spectral and ranging sensors Thermal, hyperspectral, SAR, radar, sonar, location streams (R) Band identity, calibration, sparsity and sensor noise Audio and acoustics Speech, music, environmental sound, waveforms (R) Sampling rate, phase, mixtures, content, speaker and environment Embodied and physiological sensing IMU, force, tactile, EEG, ECG, EMG, PPG (R) Body/sensor topology, units, synchronization, privacy Biomedical and records images X-ray, CT, MRI, pathology (R); notes, labs, EHR events (R/C) Anatomy, protocol, patient time, missingness, provenance Temporal and event data Regular/irregular series, trajectories, point processes, logs (R/S) Timestamps, magnitude, units, variable identity, event marks Relational and structured data Graphs, knowledge graphs, hypergraphs, relational tables (S) Permutation symmetry, typed edges, schema, hierarchy, cardinality Scientific and measurements sequences DNA/RNA, proteins, omics, molecules, spectra (R/S) Alphabet and long-range structure, assay context, physical units Compound ments and interfaces docuVisual documents, slides, charts, web pages, GUIs, maps (C) Text, pixels, layout, reading order, interaction, provenance BERT, CodeBERT, GraphCodeBERT, MetaTransformer (Devlin et al., 2019; Feng et al., 2020; Guo et al., 2021; Zhang et al., 2023c) VideoMAE, UniBind, 4M21 (Tong et al., 2022; Lyu et al., 2024; Bachmann et al., 2024) ViTImageBind, PointNet++, Lens, MeshCNN (Girdhar et al., 2023; Lei et al., 2024; Qi et al., 2017b; Hanocka et al., 2019) SatMAE, BEVFusion (Cong et al., 2022; Liu et al., 2023d) wav2vec CLAP, 2.0, MAEB (Baevski et al., 2020; Elizalde et al., 2023; Assadi et al., 2026a) ImageBind, CodeBind, MultiBench (Girdhar et al., 2023; Chen et al., 2026f; Liang et al., 2021) BiomedCLIP, Found (Zhang 2023a; Zhou et al., 2023b) TS2Vec, PatchTST, RMTPP (Yue et al., 2022; Nie et al., 2023; Du et al., 2016) GraphSAGE, Graphormer, Meta-Transformer (Hamilton et al., 2017; Ying et al., 2021; Zhang et al., 2023c) Protein LM, Geneformer, MoleculeSTM (Rives et al., 2021; Theodoris et al., 2023; Liu et al., 2023c) ColPali, MMEB-style deployment (Faysse tasks et al., 2025) RETal., et Audio: factor superposition. What distinguishes audio is not its geometry but its superposition of factors. three-second utterance simultaneously encodes what was said (content), who said it (speaker), how they said it (prosody and emotion), in what language, in what room, through what microphone, and increasingly the speakers health and affective state. These factors are not hierarchy of abstractionas in vision, where edges compose into textures and textures into objectsbut distinct factors coexisting in one waveform. Different tasks require different factors preserved and the rest destroyed, and whether given factor is recoverable at all depends on the recording, the supervision, and the evaluation protocol. The defining consequence is that there is no such thing as the embedding of an audio clip: request to embed audio is incomplete until the factor is named (Snyder et al., 2018; Baevski et al., 2020; Desplanques et al., 2020), which is why the SUPERB protocol scores learned weighted sum over layers rather than the final one 45 Omnimodal Embeddings Table 7: Factors superposed in an audio signal, representative encoder families, and factor-specific evaluation. The rows are task-conditioned views of the same input rather than mutually exclusive latent variables. The table is the empirical form of the audio-specific difference (Section 9): success in one row may require suppressing information rewarded in anotherso the audio embedding is undefined until the factor is named. Factor Representative encoder Kept by Scored by Linguistic content Speaker tity idenProsody emotion & SSL frame features (Baevski et al., 2020; Hsu et al., 2021; Chen et al., 2022a); semantic codec tokens (Huang et al., 2024b) i-vector (Dehak et al., 2011), x-vector (Snyder et al., 2018), (DesplanECAPA-TDNN ques et al., 2020), contentdisentangled speaker embeddings (Tu et al., 2024) embedProsody/timbre dings (Gengembre et al., 2024); emotion representations (Ma et al., 2024b) Recognition, translation, keyword spotting, voice activity detection Word/phone error rate for recognition; accuracy for keyword spotting Verification, diarization, targetspeaker extraction, voice cloning EER/minDCF for verification; DER for diarization Expressive synthesis, affect recognition, punctuation restoration Classification accuracy, listener studies Language & accent Language embeddings (Nam et al., 2023) Language identification, multilingual routing Identification accuracy Channel & environment Session or environment embeddings (Nam et al., 2024) Acoustic detail Neural codec residuals (Zeghidour et al., 2022; Défossez et al., 2023) Enhancement and dereverberation; removed for robust verification Downstream robustness Reconstruction and generative decoding Perceptual quality, bitrate the representation is not layer but choice over layers. Table 7 makes this concrete: it maps each audio factor to representative encoder family, the tasks that keep it, and the metrics that score it, exposing the asymmetry that success in one row may require suppressing information rewarded in another. Audio confronted the task-dependence of similarity two decades before the other modalities, and necessitated distinct family of objectives that certify factor is absent speaker removal, anonymization, and privacy-preserving speech representations (Wang et al., 2024e; Ruggiero et al., 2025; Vecino et al., 2025; Baser et al., 2025)together with tokenizers that separate content stream from an acoustic one, so that downstream generation model can keep the words while changing the speaker (Zhang et al., 2023b; Défossez et al., 2024). joint embedding must name the factor it is encoding, or preserve them as superposition it can separate on demand rather than single entangled point. Graph: explicit relational structure and non-Euclidean geometry. Graph embeddings differ from text, vision, audio, and time series because relations are part of the represented object, not side effect of an ordered signal (Bronstein et al., 2021). graph object begins from entities plus relationsedges, paths, types, weights, directions, hyperedges, temporal links, schema constraints, or higher-order substructuresand the embedding must preserve task-relevant relations while remaining insensitive to arbitrary node naming, i.e., permutation equivariant. Graph specificity may reside in arity, curvature, invariance, dynamics, or topology rather than in vectors alone: higher-arity knowledge beyond binary edges (Xiong et al., 2023; Kim et al., 2024b), non-Euclidean (hyperbolic/Lorentz) geometry for hierarchy and curvature (Lin et al., 2023c), and sign/basisinvariant spectral embeddings so that comparison is not an artifact of node ordering (Lim et al., 2023; Ma et al., 2023). The same encoder can be trained under contrastive, masked, or proximity objectives, but the learning signal is whatever operation preserves the relational unit (Chen et al., 46 Omnimodal Embeddings 2024c; Yang et al., 2024a), and Graph Transformer is graph mechanism only when relational structure is explicitly encoded into its tokenization, attention biases, or positional signal (Yuan et al., 2026). joint embedding must treat relations as representational object to be preserved, not context to be projected away. Tables: grid geometry, typed cells, and the two-readings problem. table is not bag of strings: its semantics live in two-dimensional, typed gridcell meaning is jointly determined by its value, its columns header and type, its rows identity, and its positional relations (merges, hierarchies, captions) (Deng et al., 2020; Iida et al., 2021). Three consequences follow. First, the natural unit is heterogeneous and multi-granularcell, row, column, and whole table are all legitimate representational objects, and model must decide which to expose (TABBIE exposes all three; TaPas aggregates evidence over cell selections) (Herzig et al., 2020; Iida et al., 2021). Second, table semantics are often relational but implicit: entity cells link to knowledge bases (masked entity recovery pretraining), and headers carry the schema (Deng et al., 2020; Yin et al., 2020)closer to graphs explicit relations than to texts linear order. Third, and most distinctively, tables suffer two-readings polarity: the same artifact is either semi-structured document (row and column geometry as semantics, for QA and retrieval) or matrix of i.i.d. feature rows (for prediction), and the two readings demand different invariancesthe document reading requires sensitivity to row/column identity; the ML reading requires insensitivity to row order (Gorishniy et al., 2021; Hollmann et al., 2023). joint embedding must state which reading it serves, or the geometry it learns will be wrong for the other. Time series: continuous axis, no standard units, magnitude semantics. Time series is indexed by continuous time and is the modality that lacks an inherent, semantically meaningful atomic unit: only the sample is given, and the sample is the level that carries no independent meaning, so window length and series boundary are modeling choices the modality must manufacture (Takens, 1981; Nie et al., 2023). While time series and audio have similar physical formulations (both 1D sampled signals), they differ fundamentally in semantic meaning. Audio is perceptual family speech, music, and bioacoustics whose semantics lie in what is heard. Time series, in the statistical sense, refers to any sequence of observations indexed by time whose meaning lies in their temporal dependenceprices, telemetry, event streams. The boundary is porousphysiological waveforms are claimed by both communities (Coppola et al., 2024; Wang et al., 2024b)but real. The continuous axis and the missing unit together produce three distinctive properties. First, the observation grid is itself variabletime series spans regular sampling, irregular clinical panels, and point processes in which the timestamps are the observation (Mei & Eisner, 2017; Shukla & Marlin, 2021; Xue et al., 2024b). Second, the recurring units are not standardized: the motifs whose recurrence carries meaning are domain-specific (a QRS complex, bearing-fault harmonic, weekday seasonality), and unlike word in text and audioa unit whose identity is fixed by convention across the whole communitya motif is defined operationally by the method that extracts it, which is why the distributional machinery that powers word2vec has no ready-made unit inventory to run on (Talukder et al., 2024; Lin et al., 2024). Thirdand most distinctivelyamplitude is semantics, and normalization discards it: the difference between 2C and 20C excursion is the entire content of the signal, yet the instance normalization that eases cross-dataset training removes it, leaving encoders trained on shape-only view with scale re-injected at the decoder (Lin et al., 2024; Germain et al., 2025). An alternative is to keep the statistics in the representation itself: NuTime attaches each windows mean and standard deviation to its normalized shape, so level survives as continuous attribute no finite vocabulary can enumerate (Lin et al., 2024). joint embedding must preserve the continuous axis and magnitude while tolerating channel permutations and units that no convention standardizes. Signals share second domain; symbols do not. One cross-cutting regularity the per-modality inventory above hides is that every family built on continuous signalaudio, time series, and visionhas found it profitable to represent in the frequency domain. Audios default front end is the spectrogram, timefrequency image (Huang et al., 2022a); time-series models locate their periodicity with the FFT before modeling, unfolding series by their intrinsic period (Wu et al., 47 Omnimodal Embeddings 2023a) or enforcing consistency between the time-domain and frequency-domain views of the same series (Zhang et al., 2022b); vision in its coordinate-based form must contend with spectral bias, and explicit Fourier-feature encodings are what let models learn high-frequency image content (Tancik et al., 2020). Graph learning, though targeting discrete structures rather than continuous signals, similarly has long-standing spectral branch built on the Laplacian eigenbasis (Ma et al., 2023; Lim et al., 2023). By contrast, for text, code, and tables Fourier machinery appears only as an imported generic basis (Lee-Thorp et al., 2022; Sergazinov et al., 2025), never as data-native spectrum; plausibly because the additive, shift-stationary structure that Fourier-type bases exploit is property of physical signals, which symbolic data lack. For an omnimodal encoder the observation has design force: it isolates genuine intersection (transform-based encoding shared by audio, image, graph, and time series) that cuts across the family boundaries this chapters inventory works withthe intersection and difference axes of our lens (Section 2.3) meeting in single regularity. Takeaway Each modality owns structural property the convergence has not abolishedand future joint embedding must design mechanisms that respect these properties rather than overlooking them. The properties are not obstacles to be engineered around; they are the information the modality carries, and the test of true omnimodal embedding is whether it preserves them while still fusing. The next chapter argues that the fastest route to building those mechanisms is not to invent each in isolation but to borrow across modalitiesthe reuse axis, where one modalitys hard-won technique becomes anothers import.

sections.title: 10 Frontier II: The Cross-Pollination Blueprint
sections.content: If Part II documented the intersections and Section 9 the differences, this chapter is the deliberate exercise of the third axis: reuse. We argue that the surest route to an omnimodal joint embedding is not for each modality to reinvent its missing machinery in isolation, but to cross-pollinateto port method hardened in one modality into another where its preconditions happen to hold. Our analysis of each modality suggests concrete opportunity map: source method target modality expected benefit. Table 8 summarizes it, marking which transfers are already documented and which remain proposed experiment, with the expected benefit spelled out for each; the rest of this section expands the most promising vectors, each of which we frame as conditional port whose preconditions must hold for the benefit to materialize. Texts instruction tuning audio and time series. Text resolved the universality/specialization tension by conditioning the embedding on task instruction (Su et al., 2023): one model produces different embeddings of the same input depending on the instruction, amortizing one trunk instead of specialist encoders and extending to factors not anticipated at training. Audios answer to its factor superposition was instead separate encoder per factor plus sprawling disentanglement literature (Lin et al., 2023a; Tu et al., 2024; Gengembre et al., 2024; Ruggiero et al., 2025). The crosspollination is direct: an audio encoder that accepts an instructionembed for speaker identity, discarding content or embed for acoustic scene, ignoring speechwould subsume the per-factor table and much of the disentanglement work, dominating on every axis (one trunk, explicit and auditable geometry, no need for explicit factor-orthogonality constraints) (Su et al., 2023; Wang et al., 2024d). The same logic reaches time series, where an instruction-conditioned series encoder is technically straightforward given the LLM-bridging work already in place (Sun et al., 2024a), and would realize by-task embedding generation for modality that currently has no instructionconditioned embedding model. Audios codec discretization code and time series. Audio entered the language-model ecosystem because neural codecs quantize waveform into discrete tokens that an autoregressive model already consumes (Zeghidour et al., 2022; Défossez et al., 2023), and semantic distillation or represen48 Omnimodal Embeddings Table 8: Bounded cross-pollination opportunity map. marks at least one use documented in this survey; proposed cross-family experiment; no clear mapping proposed here. Open circles make no absence claim. Rows are grouped by the source family in which the method was hardened, without claiming unique origin. The rightmost column states the expected benefit of the transfer when the targets preconditions hold (drawn from the pollination analysis of Section 10); transfer is directed and conditional, not free transplant. Method (source family) Text Vision Audio Series Graph Tabular Expected benefit From text Instruction-conditioned embedding (Su et al., 2023; Wang et al., 2024d) Nested (Matryoshka) representations (Kusupati et al., 2022) Late interaction / multi-vector readout (Faysse et al., 2025) Relevance-judged contrastive supervision (Xiong et al., 2021) Frozen-trunk benchmark across heterogeneous tasks (Conneau & Kiela, 2018; Muennighoff et al., 2023) From audio Statistics pooling (second moment) (Snyder et al., 2018) Attack-and-utility evaluation after factor suppression (Ruggiero et al., 2025; Vecino et al., 2025) Layer-wise probing as pretraining diagnostic (Yang et al., 2021) From graph Declared symmetry enforced architecturally (Germain et al., 2025; Ying et al., 2021) Structural (non-positional) position encoding (Ying et al., 2021) Permutation-equivariant treatment of channel set (Kipf & Welling, 2017) From time series Scale-factorized numeric embedding (Lin et al., 2024) Continuous-time index rather than integer positions (Shukla & Marlin, 2021; Fraikin et al., 2024; Mei & Eisner, 2017; Xu et al., 2020a) Entity-keyed groups positives or From tabular / table column idenCross-dataset tity derived from descriptions (Deng et al., 2020; Yin et al., 2020) One amortized trunk replaces perfactor/per-task encoders; makes the requested geometry explicit and auditable Cheap storageaccuracy dial shared across modalities at serve time Recovers localized evidence global vector collapses Sharpens distinctions coarse in-batch negatives miss Makes better embedding operationally meaningful, decoupled from decoder Retains the variability that separates steady signal from an erratic one Turns this embedding does not contain into an auditable property Reveals which representation state task actually consumes States the invariance group in the model rather than guessing it via augmentation Adds topology/centrality without imposing false linear lattice Treats rows/variables as an unordered set, not fixed axis Places numerals (2 vs. 20) and absolute levels in metric relation where current embeddings fail Handles variable-rate video and dynamic graphs natively Declares same instance/state rather than generic augmentation Aligns channel across datasets that share units but not schema tation quantization later separated semantic tokens from acoustic detail (Zhang et al., 2023b; Huang et al., 2024b). The transferable idea is learned semantic codebooks, and it has two natural targets. For code, discretizing execution traces into token sequences could let code embedding models jointly learn from source text and behavioral semantics, aligning function with its trace the way codec aligns audio with its content (Huang et al., 2024a). For time series, learned codebook is the path to language-model treatmentand indeed has been attempted with byte-pair encoding over quantized 49 Omnimodal Embeddings values (Götz et al., 2025) and learned VQ (Talukder et al., 2024), whose generalist codebook transfers to domains that share no sampling rate or sensor with its training data. The precondition flagged by audio is that discretization requires recurring unitswhether attested phones for speech codec, learned acoustic labels for BEATs (Chen et al., 2023c), or data-native codes for TOTEM (Talukder et al., 2024). What none of these cases settles is what the vocabulary means away from its training corpus: tokens defined per corpus need not denote the same thing across domains, so the import test is whether vocabularyattested or learnedsustains stable recurring units on the target signal. Reuse, here, comes with that precondition test, because recurrence, not signal shape, is what the method was built on. Where no stable units form, magnitude-preserving numeric embedding (Lin et al., 2024) is the more faithful bridge. Graphs structural modeling text and code. Graphs export is relational abstraction as structural layer. Edgeformers, for example, couples edge text with network context for node and edge representation learning (Jin et al., 2023a). Related ideas are already established in code: GraphCodeBERT incorporates data-flow structure (Guo et al., 2021), while CGM integrates repository-level code graphs into language modeling (Tao et al., 2025). These examples motivate further study of when explicit relations, such as citation links or code dependencies, improve embeddings beyond content alone. The transferable lesson here is the graph sections discipline: name the represented unit and the relational objective before comparing architectures (Khoshraftar & An, 2024; Wang et al., 2024a). Graphs structural modeling is thus complementary relational layer over other modalities. Time series continuous-time indexing video and dynamic graphs. Every modality is acquiring time axisvariable-rate video, continuous-time dynamic graphs, time-scoped retrievaland most still treat time as positional encoding over integers, the approximation time series abandoned decade ago for representations defined on (Mei & Eisner, 2017; Kazemi et al., 2019; Shukla & Marlin, 2021; Fraikin et al., 2024; Walker et al., 2026). For continuous-time dynamic graphs the crossing has already happened: TGAT learns node embeddings as functions of continuous time, with functional time encoding derived from Bochners theorem (Xu et al., 2020a). Time series therefore exports its coordinate: the machinery for continuous-time embeddings, multi-time attention, and learned timeembeddings that handle irregular sampling natively. The expected benefits are concrete: variablespeed video understanding without frame re-sampling, and temporal knowledge-graph embeddings that move beyond treating timestamps as isolated discrete identifiers (Li et al., 2023b; Gao et al., 2023b) to full continuous-time functions. The broader position is that in any real omnimodal setting (a patient with waveforms, labs, imaging, and notes; vehicle with telemetry, camera, and events) modalities are co-observed on common clock, and the binding relation should be temporal cooccurrence, with time series supplying and encoding the axisnot the hub, but the coordinate system the hub is expressed in. Factor accounting vision and text. Audios most transferable contribution may be methodological rather than architectural: factor table that lists, for each factor over an input, which embedding space keeps it, which removes it, and how each is scored (Snyder et al., 2018; Baevski et al., 2020; Desplanques et al., 2020; Défossez et al., 2023), with removal metrics that make this embedding does not contain testable (Ruggiero et al., 2025; Vecino et al., 2025; Baser et al., 2025). This template is not an audio artifact: any modality whose inputs superpose distinct factors can build it, converting similarity is task-dependent into per-factor list with metrics. Visions appearance-vs-identity factors and texts content-vs-style factors (sarcasm, sentiment, register) both admit such table, and importing audios removal-objective family would turn factor control from an ad hoc finetuning trick into an auditable property of the embedding. Takeaway The pattern across these vectors is that reuse is directed and conditional, not free transplant. Each port succeeds when the target modality satisfies the methods preconditionsa recurring unit inventory for discretization, relation as the represented object for structural 50 Omnimodal Embeddings modeling, continuous axis for continuous-time indexingand fails, predictably, when it does not. The cross-pollination that respects these preconditions is, we argue, the most efficient route to joint embedding that masters each modalitys distinctive property: not by reinventing solution per modality, but by routing each modality to the community that has already solved its problem.

sections.title: 11 Evaluation: We Cannot Build What We Cannot Measure
sections.content: The third level of fragmentationafter research and surveys (Section 1.1)is evaluation, and it is the binding constraint on the whole enterprise: until there is shared yardstick, claims about which convergence has occurred and which model is more omnimodal remain unfalsifiable. This chapter surveys the modality-specific instruments, diagnoses what they cannot measure, and lays out what unified omnimodal benchmark must contain and what stands in the way of building it, using the 3C lenscoverage, comparability, and compositionalityas the scale on which any omnimodal claim is weighed. To do that we first make the three capabilities explicit. Table 9 states the question each capability answers and the minimum evidence it requires, and crucially the shortcuts routinely mistaken for itcounting tokenizers, shared backbone, co-occurrence, or task accuracy. Table 10 then decouples mechanism (transformation, shared backbone, alignment, joint fusion) from capability: check mark means mechanism can support capability, not that it has been demonstrated. This separation is the backbone of the evaluation argument: system that scores on coverage does not thereby score on comparability or compositionality. Islands of evaluation. Most modalities have each matured their own frozen-encoder benchmark. Text has MTEB (Muennighoff et al., 2023) and its multilingual extension MMTEB (Enevoldsen et al., 2025), with retrieval suites BEIR (Thakur et al., 2021), AIR-Bench (Chen et al., 2025b), the enterprise-domain RTEB (Liu et al., 2025a), and reasoning-intensive suites like BRIGHT (Su et al., 2025) that expose sharp gap (a model scoring 59.0 on MTEB can drop to 18.3 on BRIGHT). Code has CoIR (Li et al., 2025e), CPRet (Deng et al., 2025), and CoREB (Xue et al., 2026a) for the full search pipeline. Audio has SUPERB (Yang et al., 2021)established in 2021, three years after texts SentEval standardized the same frozen-encoder probing (Conneau & Kiela, 2018)and its successors HEAR for general audio (Turian et al., 2021), MARBLE for music (Yuan et al., 2023), AV-SUPERB for audio-visual (Tseng et al., 2024), the unified X-ARES (Zhang et al., 2025a), and the MTEB-style MSEB (Heigold et al., 2025) and MAEB (Assadi et al., 2026a). Vision has classification, retrieval, and detection suites (Russakovsky et al., 2015; Radenovic et al., 2018), now aggregated in the MTEB-style MIEB (Xiao et al., 2025b), with the successively harder ViDoRe line covering visual document retrieval (Faysse et al., 2025; Macé et al., 2025; Loison et al., 2026), and MVEB extending the frozen-encoder discipline to video (Assadi et al., 2026b). Graph evaluation spans node, link, and graph-property prediction in OGB (Hu et al., 2020a), structural stress tests such as LRGB (Dwivedi et al., 2022), and cross-dataset transfer benchmarks for graph foundation models (Chen et al., 2024f; Yu et al., 2026). Tables are scored through task heads rather than an embedding suite: table QA, fact verification, and text-to-SQL over WikiTableQuestions, TabFact, and Spider (Pasupat & Liang, 2015; Yu et al., 2018; Chen et al., 2020c; Zhou et al., 2024a), with MTEB-style frozen-encoder analogs (TEmBed, TabBench, TRL-Bench) only now appearing (Vogel et al., 2026; Qiang et al., 2026; Pang et al., 2026). Time series is the outlier: encoders there are evaluated through end-toend forecasting metrics (Aksu et al., 2024; Xue et al., 2026b)or through frozen-representation classification probes on UCR/UEA (Bagnall et al., 2018; Dau et al., 2019), but neither strand has consolidated into broadly adopted MTEB analog. Cross-modal retrieval is where the aggregation effort has concentrated most recently: the M-BEIR and MMEB suites (Wei et al., 2024a; Jiang et al., 2025), which assemble long-standing textimage retrieval benchmarks (Lin et al., 2014), have been extended by MMEB-V2 (adding video and visual documents; Xu et al., 2016; Meng et al., 2026) and MMEB-V3 (adding audio and agent retrieval; Huang et al., 2026a), while MixBench targets the mixed-modality corpus in which texts, images, and text-plus-image documents must be retrieved 51 Omnimodal Embeddings Table 9: The three capabilities (the 3C lens) an omnimodal embedding claim must demonstrate. Each capability requires separate evidence; they should not be collapsed into one score. The insufficient evidence column lists shortcuts that are routinely mistaken for capability but establish none. The three are progressively stronger, mirroring the paths of Sections 6 to 8. For which input sets does the result depend on all inputs? Mechanisms are listed in order of interaction depth, and the last column states what an evaluation must still test. This decouples what the model does (a mechanism) from what it is good for (a capability). What the silos cannot measure. Three limitations follow from this fragmentation. First, the benchmark silos encode decoder-coupling problem by omission: better embedding has operational meaning in text (because MTEB scores frozen encoder independent of decoder), but not in time series benchmarks that report joint properties of encoder and forecast head (Aksu et al., 2024; Xue et al., 2026b). modality-drop/conflict; pairing noise; calibration; component attribution the head is sized, and no suite standardizes this convincingly (Zaiem et al., 2023; Hallap et al., 2023; van Merriënboer et al., 2025). Third, and most consequentially, no existing benchmark is truly omnimodal: MTEB and SUPERB are unimodal, the cross-modal suites (M-BEIR, MMEB, and its V2/V3 extensions) are bito few-modal, and none measures single embedding models performance across all modalities under one protocol. Indeed, recent analysis of MAEB finds that across 53 encoders and 30 tasks no single model dominates, with clean double dissociation (contrastive audio-text models strong on environmental sound but near-random on multilingual speech, and vice versa)precisely the kind of finding no unimodal silo could surface (Assadi et al., 2026a). The instruments that do exist for compositionality are deliberately narrow diagnostics: Winoground (Thrush et al., 2022), ARO (Yüksekgönül et al., 2023), and SugarCrepe (Hsieh et al., 53 Omnimodal Embeddings 2023) expose how badly visionlanguage encoders mishandle word order, attribution, and binding state-of-the-art models score close to chance on Winogrounds captionimage swapsbut they are bimodal contrast sets rather than embedding suites, and none extends to third modality, let alone to omnimodal fusion: C3 remains the least measured of the three capabilities. Toward unified omnimodal benchmark. benchmark capable of evaluating true joint embedding should specify three dimensions. Multimodal inputs. The benchmark must cover Text, Code, Image, Video, Audio, Graph, Table, and Time Seriesboth individually and in combinationso that single model can be scored on every modality it claims to handle, and on the cross-modal pairs it claims to fuse. Multi-task types. It must span at least three families: unimodal tasks (retrieval, classification, similarity) per modality, cross-modal retrieval (text-to-image, audio-to-text, query-to-timeseries), and multimodal fusion tasks in which the input itself is multimodal (multimodal question answering, composed image retrieval (Vo et al., 2019; Saito et al., 2023; Gao et al., 2026), audio-visual event recognition). Critically, it must include compositional gain controls: joint embedding should beat the strongest unimodal encoder and the additive baselines of score fusion and vector addition, with unimodal ablations and feature-fusion controls, or the fusion is not doing work (Jiang et al., 2025) (we formalize this requirement as the metric comp below). unified evaluation protocol. All modalities and tasks must use the frozen-encoder, deliberately-weak-head protocol that made MTEB and SUPERB credible (Yang et al., 2021; Muennighoff et al., 2023), with standardized (and reported) probe budget, intrinsic diagnostics (alignmentuniformity (Wang & Isola, 2020), anisotropy (Ethayarajh, 2019), inversion attacks (Morris et al., 2023)), andnon-negotiable for time seriesa decoder-independent retrieval instrument that makes better embedding operational without coupling it to forecast head. An operational metric for C3. So far compositionality has been verbal criterionbeats the best single/subset input, score fusion, and vector addition  (Table 9)  and verbal criteria do not make it onto leaderboards. To give the third form benchmark can adopt directly, we propose that every task whose input spans modalities x1, . . . , xk report the compositional gain comp = Perf(cid:0) fθ(x1, . . . , xk)(cid:1) max Perf(cid:0) fθ(xS)(cid:1), Perf(cid:0)i wi fθ(xi)(cid:1), Perf(cid:0)i visi (cid:1)(cid:111) , (5) (cid:110) max S{1,...,k} where fθ is the frozen embedding model, Perf higher-is-better utility derived from the task metric (evaluated over either vector representation or candidate ranking score), xS = {xi}iS nonempty proper subset of the 2 inputs, si the retrieval score that the separately encoded xi assigns to candidate, and the two sets of fusion weights and fitted on validation split so that neither side can tune the baselines in its favor. model earns C3 credit on task only where comp > 0. leaderboard column reporting the fraction of tasks and modality subsets with positive gain is then comparable across systems, and degenerates gracefully to 0 for pairwise cross-modal suites where each query or candidate item is unimodal (k = 1). comp is motivated by the synergy term of the partial information decomposition (PID) of Liang et al. (2023a), which decomposes the information that several inputs carry about target into redundant, unique, and synergistic parts, the synergistic part arising only from the joint variable. However, this parallel is not an equivalence: PID is property of the data distribution, whereas comp measures the end-to-end performance of one frozen model, so positive value attests gain over the specified baselines, not the presence of synergistic information. The design principles that MSEB articulated for audio are those an omnimodal benchmark must inherit: prioritize tasks with real applicability, measure efficiency as first-class quantity alongside accuracy, include retrieval and reasoning rather than classification alone, and require that evaluation involve no task-specific finetuning (Heigold et al., 2025). Omnimodal Embeddings Why such benchmark is hard to build. The specification above is easy to state and hard to realize, because the real-world scenarios that most need multimodal fusion happen to be the ones that resist being frozen into public benchmark. Fusion data is expensive to label and rarely releasable. The compositional tasks that matter most are the most expensive to label: constructing composed image retrieval benchmarks is expensive and time-consuming (Huynh et al., 2025), some benchmarks turned out noisy enough that later work had to re-label and prune them (Huynh et al., 2025), and expert-level multimodal benchmarks have to recruit dozens of annotators with domain expertise (Yue et al., 2024; Xue et al., 2024a). As result, most aggregation benchmarks reuse labels collected for older datasets instead of commissioning new ones (Wei et al., 2024a). Meanwhile, the scenarios that genuinely fuse modalitiesclinical encounters, meetings, vehicle fleetsare locked behind privacy and licensing regimes: audio must be anonymized before it can be shared at all (Tomashenko et al., 2022), medical imaging paired with free-text reports becomes public only after institutional de-identification (Johnson et al., 2019), and license tags are simply unspecified for over 70% of popular datasets on the major hosting platforms (Longpre et al., 2023)already enough sprawl that MMTEB had to prune tasks with underspecified licenses (Enevoldsen et al., 2025). benchmark assembled from whatever happens to be releasable will systematically underrepresent exactly the fusion settings that matter most. Multimodal scores admit unimodal shortcuts and contamination. Multimodal benchmarks repeatedly turn out to admit single-modality priors: balancing VQA against language priors exposed that top-performing models had been relying on shortcut rules (Goyal et al., 2017), and shortcuts that win on standard benchmarks while failing under real-world shift are the documented general failure mode (Geirhos et al., 2020). The compositional-gain controls above are therefore necessity rather than nicetyand since deployed sensors drop out and inputs are noisy, robustness to missing and corrupted modalities must be scored axis, not an afterthought (Liang et al., 2021). Public test sets are also moving target: evaluation has been declared in trouble unless contamination is measured for each benchmark (Sainz et al., 2023), and the MTEB maintenance effort already documents popular embedding models trained on data from the same distributions as benchmark tasks (Chung et al., 2025). Measuring is expensive and static snapshots go stale. Evaluating model on text-only suite is already costly enough that MMTEB had to down-sample datasets and curate hard negatives to keep evaluation affordable (Enevoldsen et al., 2025), and an omnimodal superset multiplies the bill across modalities. Static snapshots also age fast: frozen suites are surpassed by models that still fail simple challenge examples (Kiela et al., 2021), which is why recent retrieval benchmarks regenerate themselves from knowledge-base deltas rather than fixing candidate set (Zhou et al., 2025a). Only sustained engineeringversioning, dataset-integrity checks, contamination detectionkeeps such resource usable at all (Chung et al., 2025). None of these difficulties is fatalthe MTEB lineage shows that licensing curation, down-sampling, and maintenance can carve usable yardstick amidst these complexities (Enevoldsen et al., 2025; Chung et al., 2025)but together they explain why the natural first drafts of an omnimodal benchmark will be aggregations of existing islands, and why aggregation alone will miss the compositional tasks that the joint-embedding claim stands or falls on. Why this matters now. The convergence of Part II and the fusion models of Part III are only as credible as the instrument that measures them. An omnimodal embedding trained without an omnimodal benchmark will, like the early audio foundation models, be optimized for tasks the benchmark prioritizes and blind to those it omitsand the double dissociations MAEB found will recur at the omnimodal scale unless the benchmark is built to expose them (Assadi et al., 2026a). Building such benchmark is prerequisite for, not consequence of, the omnimodal embedding; until it exists, the most central claim of this paperthat joint embedding unifies and surpasses alignmentis, strictly, hypothesis rather than measured fact. 55 Omnimodal Embeddings Coverage test direct encoding for each claimed input type Comparability test both retrieval directions and bias Compositionality outperform single-input & baselines (comp > 0) Deployment test robustness, cost, safety, and updates each claimed input + scale; frozen or fixed-budget probe held-out pairs; same candidates; query and modality bias redundancy + complementarity; conflict + missing inputs bytes + latency; uncertainty; cross-version retrieval Figure 7: Evidence required for broader claims. Omnimodal results must report the three 3C capabilitiescoverage, comparability, and compositionalitywithin their declared scope, followed by deployment checks (robustness, cost, safety, and cross-version compatibility). The gates list increasing evidence requirements, not required processing pipeline. Table 12: Evidence for systems selected for broad input support or alignment. Coverage (C1) and Comparability (C2) are the focus; the Compositionality (C3) column only records whether the same work reports any multi-input evidence. denotes direct testing, partial testing, and dash an untested requirement. The table separates parameter reuse from cross-modal retrieval: sharing backbone and matching separately encoded inputs are different capabilities. comparing two non-image inputs is not fusion Supports broad conditional generation, but not general dense retrieval vector Multiple 2D, 3D, video, audio and sensor inputs Adapters map new inputs into existing aligned spaces Evaluation covers only subset of possible input pairs Language-centered image, video and related retrieval tasks MLLM state alignment plus contrastive refinement Multilingual text and images Universal retrieval vectors e5-omni et al., 2026b) (Chen Text, image, video and audio image, audio and Text, video suite Temperature calibration, negative mining, and covariance alignment Separately aligned encoders that preserve the text space D Text, image, video, documents and audio Specialist projector recovery fusion plus CodeBind (Chen et al., 2026f) Nine modalities incl. tactile, 3D and EEG Separate alignment with compositional codebook Improved cross-modal comparison does not establish arbitrary multi-input composition Tested imagetext combinations do not establish broader multiinput composition The main evidence concerns calibration and cross-modal comparison Extends the space efficiently, but does not evaluate joint composition of all four inputs Adding specialists can shift stored embeddings and degrade retrieval compatibility Testing many pairs does not demonstrate joint fusion of all nine modalities 4M-21 (Bachmann et al., 2024) / ViT-Lens UniBind (Lei et al., 2024; Lyu et al., 2024) LCOEmbedding (Xiao et al., 2025a) jina-embeddingsv4 (Günther et al., 2025) jina-embeddingsv5-omni (Hönicke et al., 2026) Conanembedding-v3 (Li et al., 2026c) What the evidence we have already shows. We can nevertheless read the current literature against the 3C lens. Figure 7 summarizes the gates an omnimodal claim must pass, from coverage through comparability and compositionality to deployment. Two evidence matrices make the gates concrete. Table 12 scores systems selected for broad input support or alignment, and shows that most of them establish coverage and comparability but not compositionality: shared backbone or hub anchor is repeatedly mistaken for fusion. Table 13 scores systems that explicitly combine several inputs; as of the review cutoff, almost all of them carry only partial (P) compositionality grade, with only single strong (D) result, which itself is restricted to just two modalities. Compositionality remains 56 Omnimodal Embeddings Table 13: Evidence for queries or candidates made from several inputs. In column C3, means that combined inputs were useful, but the study did not include all of the baselines and stress tests needed for stronger claim; means direct compositional-gain evidence against single-input and simple-fusion baselines. As of the review cutoff, compositionality remains the least established capability.
